articles.author: Jakub Gawlik
articles.description:
Why we built a team workspace around one question: what does a fully compromised server learn?
Most “private” workspace tools protect your data with a promise. The promise lives in a privacy policy: we will not look, we will not sell, we will not share. It may be sincere. But a promise is only as strong as the people keeping it, the staff who can reach the database, and the next attacker who gets in.
lockORG takes a different approach. It is a workspace app (notes, kanban boards, tags, todos and a journal) for small teams and individuals, and everything in it is encrypted on your device before it is sent. The server stores it, syncs it, and never reads it. Nor can it.
That is the difference between a promise and a property. A promise can be broken. A property is how the system is built.
Ev…
articles.title: A Privacy Policy is a promise. Zero-knowledge is a property.

Big O Notation


Vamos logo falar da notação que vai nos acompanhar a carreira inteira. Big O é uma forma de denotar o desempenho de um algoritmo, levando sempre em consideração o pior dos casos. Porém, Big O leva em consideração a escalabilidade e a execução. Por exemplo, O(n) é melhor que O(n²), mas, sem a análise assintótica, não podemos afirmar com total certeza. Análise assintótica é a forma de avaliar o algoritmo conforme o tamanho da entrada cresce. 
A análise assintótica é utilizada para avaliar o desempenho e a eficiência de um algoritmo à medida que o tamanho da entrada de uma função cresce indefinidamente, aproximando-se do infinito. Isso é feito já que medir pelo tempo exato cria muitas variantes e inconsistências, como a velocidade do processador da máquina.

articles.author: Stefano Franco
articles.description:
On 21 October 2026 the PHP project fixed two critical bugs, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, quickly nicknamed php2shell. Both can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. In the first, an out-of-memory error can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized; request parsing is the easiest way to get there, but not the only one. In the second, request-owned state survives in a persistent worker after its memory has been freed. Full RCE was demonstrated on Apache mod_php; on PHP-FPM the exposure is more limited and depends on the configuration, but "limited" is not "safe".
The fixed releases were 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12, and the PHP project published minimal source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1. Anything older depends on distributions and LTS pro…
